**CAVA Compilation Instructions**

**1. Install Dependencies**

*   **Required:**
    *   FFTW (http://www.fftw.org/)
    *   libtool
    *   automake
    *   pkgconf
    *   build-essentials
    *   iniparser (https://github.com/ndevilla/iniparser)

*   **Recommended (for audio capture):**
    *   Development libraries for one of the following audio frameworks: ALSA, Pulseaudio, Pipewire, Portaudio, Sndio, or JACK.
    *   *Note: On macOS, Core Audio is supported natively.*

*   **Optional:**
    *   SDL2 dev files
    *   autoconf-archive (for OpenGL)
    *   ncursesw dev files (alternative output method)

**Platform-Specific Dependency Installation:**

*   **FreeBSD:**
    ```bash
    pkg install autoconf automake fftw3 iniparser jackit libglvnd libtool pkgconf psftools sdl2 sndio
    export CFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include"
    export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib"
    ```

*   **Debian/Ubuntu:**
    ```bash
    sudo apt install build-essential libfftw3-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libtool automake libiniparser-dev libsdl2-2.0-0 libsdl2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libjack-jackd2-dev pkgconf
    ```

*   **ArchLinux:**
    ```bash
    pacman -S base-devel fftw alsa-lib iniparser pulseaudio pkgconf
    ```

*   **openSUSE:**
    ```bash
    zypper install alsa-devel fftw3-devel libpulse-devel libtool pkgconf
    ```

*   **Fedora:**
    ```bash
    dnf install alsa-lib-devel fftw3-devel pulseaudio-libs-devel libtool iniparser-devel pkgconf
    ```

*   **macOS:**
    1.  Install Homebrew if not already installed.
    2.  Install prerequisites:
        ```bash
        brew install fftw libtool automake pkgconf portaudio iniparser
        ```
    3.  Fix libtool path issues:
        ```bash
        export LIBTOOL=`which glibtool`
        export LIBTOOLIZE=`which glibtoolize`
        ln -s `which glibtoolize` /usr/local/bin/libtoolize
        ```
    4.  *Apple Silicon only:* Set flags for Homebrew packages:
        ```bash
        export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/lib"
        export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/include"
        ```

*   **Windows:**
    *   **Option A (vcpkg + CMake):**
        ```bash
        cmake --preset vcpkg
        cd build
        cmake --build . --config Release
        ```
    *   **Option B (MSYS2/MinGW):**
        ```bash
        pacboy cc cmake fftw glew ninja SDL2
        cmake -bin
        cmake --build bin
        ```

**2. Build the Project**

Clone the repository and navigate to the project directory.

*   **Linux/macOS (Autoconf/Automake - Default):**
    ```bash
    ./autogen.sh
    ./configure
    make
    ```
    *   *Note:* You can disable specific features during `./configure` if needed (see `./configure --help`).

*   **Windows (CMake):**
    Use the CMake commands specified in the Windows dependency section above.

**3. Install**

*   **Default Installation (to `/usr/local`):**
    ```bash
    make install
    ```

*   **Custom Prefix:**
    ```bash
    ./configure --prefix=/your/custom/path
    make
    make install
    ```

**4. Uninstall**

```bash
make uninstall
```

**CAVA Compilation Instructions**

**1. Install Dependencies**

*   **Required:**
    *   FFTW (http://www.fftw.org/)
    *   libtool
    *   automake
    *   pkgconf
    *   build-essentials
    *   iniparser (https://github.com/ndevilla/iniparser)

*   **Recommended (for audio capture):**
    *   Development libraries for one of the following audio frameworks: ALSA, Pulseaudio, Pipewire, Portaudio, Sndio, or JACK.
    *   *Note: On macOS, Core Audio is supported natively.*

*   **Optional:**
    *   SDL2 dev files
    *   autoconf-archive (for OpenGL)
    *   ncursesw dev files (alternative output method)

**Platform-Specific Dependency Installation:**

*   **FreeBSD:**
    ```bash
    pkg install autoconf automake fftw3 iniparser jackit libglvnd libtool pkgconf psftools sdl2 sndio
    export CFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include"
    export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib"
    ```

*   **Debian/Ubuntu:**
    ```bash
    sudo apt install build-essential libfftw3-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libtool automake libiniparser-dev libsdl2-2.0-0 libsdl2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libjack-jackd2-dev pkgconf
    ```

*   **ArchLinux:**
    ```bash
    pacman -S base-devel fftw alsa-lib iniparser pulseaudio pkgconf
    ```

*   **openSUSE:**
    ```bash
    zypper install alsa-devel fftw3-devel libpulse-devel libtool pkgconf
    ```

*   **Fedora:**
    ```bash
    dnf install alsa-lib-devel fftw3-devel pulseaudio-libs-devel libtool iniparser-devel pkgconf
    ```

*   **macOS:**
    1.  Install Homebrew if not already installed.
    2.  Install prerequisites:
        ```bash
        brew install fftw libtool automake pkgconf portaudio iniparser
        ```
    3.  Fix libtool path issues:
        ```bash
        export LIBTOOL=`which glibtool`
        export LIBTOOLIZE=`which glibtoolize`
        ln -s `which glibtoolize` /usr/local/bin/libtoolize
        ```
    4.  *Apple Silicon only:* Set flags for Homebrew packages:
        ```bash
        export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/lib"
        export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/include"
        ```

*   **Windows:**
    *   **Option A (vcpkg + CMake):**
        ```bash
        cmake --preset vcpkg
        cd build
        cmake --build . --config Release
        ```
    *   **Option B (MSYS2/MinGW):**
        ```bash
        pacboy cc cmake fftw glew ninja SDL2
        cmake -bin
        cmake --build bin
        ```

**2. Build the Project**

Clone the repository and navigate to the project directory.

*   **Linux/macOS (Autoconf/Automake - Default):**
    ```bash
    ./autogen.sh
    ./configure
    make
    ```
    *   *Note:* You can disable specific features during `./configure` if needed (see `./configure --help`).

*   **Windows (CMake):**
    Use the CMake commands specified in the Windows dependency section above.

**3. Install**

*   **Default Installation (to `/usr/local`):**
    ```bash
    make install
    ```

*   **Custom Prefix:**
    ```bash
    ./configure --prefix=/your/custom/path
    make
    make install
    ```

**4. Uninstall**

```bash
make uninstall
```

Only FFTW, iniparser and the build tools are actually required for CAVA to compile, but this will only give you the ability to read from fifo files. To capture audio directly from your system, additional audio development files may be needed depending on your input backend (pipewire, pulseaudio, alsa, sndio, jack or portaudio). On macOS, the built-in Core Audio framework is supported without extra audio capture libraries.

Ncurses can be used as an alternative output method if you have issues with the default one. But it is not required.

Introduction
FFTW
is a C
subroutine library for computing the discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
in one or more dimensions, of arbitrary input size, and of both real
and complex data (as well as of even/odd data, i.e. the discrete
cosine/sine transforms or DCT/DST).  We believe that FFTW,
which is
free software
, should become the
FFT
library of choice for most
applications.
The latest official release of FFTW is version
3.3.11
,
available from
our download page
.  Version
3.3 introduced support for the AVX x86 extensions, a
distributed-memory implementation on top of MPI, and a Fortran 2003
API.  Version 3.3.1 introduced support for the ARM Neon
extensions. See the
release notes
for
more information.
The FFTW package was developed at
MIT
by
Matteo Frigo
and
Steven G.  Johnson
.
Our
benchmarks
,
performed on on a variety of platforms, show that FFTW's performance
is typically superior to that of other publicly available FFT
software, and is even competitive with vendor-tuned codes.  In
contrast to vendor-tuned codes, however, FFTW's performance is
portable
: the same program will perform well on most
architectures without modification. Hence the name, "FFTW," which
stands for the somewhat whimsical title of "
Fastest Fourier
Transform in the West
."
Subscribe to
the
fftw-announce
mailing list
to receive release announcements (or use the web feed
).
Features
FFTW 3.3.11 is the latest official version of FFTW (refer to the
release notes
to find out what is new).
Here is a list of some of FFTW's more interesting features:
Speed.
(Supports SSE/SSE2/Altivec, since version
3.0.  Version 3.3.1 supports AVX and ARM Neon.)
Both one-dimensional and
multi-dimensional
transforms.
Arbitrary-size
transforms.  (Sizes with small prime factors are
best, but FFTW uses O(N log N) algorithms even for prime sizes.)
Fast transforms of
purely real
input or output data.
Transforms of real even/odd data: the
discrete cosine transform
(DCT) and the
discrete sine transform
(DST), types I-IV.  (Version 3.0 or later.)
Efficient handling of
multiple, strided
transforms. (This lets you
do things like transform multiple arrays at once, transform one
dimension of a multi-dimensional array, or transform one field of a
multi-component array.)
Parallel transforms
: parallelized
code for platforms with
SMP
machines with some flavor
of
threads
(e.g. POSIX) or
OpenMP
. An
MPI
version for distributed-memory transforms is
also available in FFTW 3.3.
Portable
to any platform with a C compiler.
Documentation
in HTML and other formats.
Both
C
and
Fortran
interfaces.
Free
software, released under the GNU General Public License (GPL, see
FFTW license
).
(Non-free licenses may also be
purchased from MIT
, for users who do not want their programs protected by
the GPL.
Contact us
for details.)  (See also the
